newsitem.title: FRANCE: Traders see lower subsidy bids at EU grain tender.
newsitem.headline: Traders see lower subsidy bids at EU grain tender.

text.p: Grain shippers expect a fall in bids for wheat export subsidies at a weekly European Union grain tender on Thursday, exporters said.
Traders are anxious to grab export certificates at what is the last auction of the year and likely to be one of its most lively, they said.
"We see less than nine Ecus," said one trader, noting this was the level bid on the secondary market for restitutions earlier on Thursday. Dollar-based wheat prices were higher.
Others said they expected heated competition for refunds ahead of a two-week break in the tender system.
At last Thursday's tender, traders bid through France for 1,322,200 tonnes of EU soft wheat from the open market at rebates of 16.47 to 21.74 Ecus per tonne.
The European Commission awarded 477,700 tonnes across the EU at a maximum rebate of 17.47 Ecus per tonne.
EU agriculture director Guy Legras said afterwards that the EU would slow down the export pace at this week's auction and reaffirmed the remarks on Monday.
Traders said refunds were bid at nine Ecus on Thursday compared with 10-11 Ecus on Tuesday.
Dollar-denominated French wheat which includes an allowance for restitutions was quoted around $160 per tonne on Thursday instead of $155 per tonne earlier in the week.
As weekly grain export bids went in to the European Commission, traders said Iraq was close to buying French wheat under its U.N. oil-for-food deal.
